title: One door
question: Why Does This Tiny Strait Matter to the World?
scoredBy: inspection of rendered frames at 0/33/66/94 per shot
verdict: The best of the five, and the reason is that the subject happens to be made of measurements. Three shots get a real drawn bar -- twenty-one miles, two miles, and the closing figure -- and those three are the only shots in the whole benchmark where the picture carries the claim instead of repeating it. cold-noir over the wash field gives a clean near-black ground that suits an oil-and-warships subject. It still shows no place, no ship and no water.
whatWorked: The measurement diagram fired three times and each one is the right graphic for its sentence.
cold-noir + wash is the strongest mood/ground pairing of the five: flat, dark, legible, unfussy.
The argument is built properly -- narrow, narrower, volume, share, no alternative, who holds it, what one accident does, what it costs -- and the 'one door' line sits at the hinge.
Hierarchy is the clearest of the five: one accent word per frame, never two.
The ending returns to the opening figure, which closes the loop rather than just stopping.

whatFailed.what: No map. A geography episode with no geography in it.
whatFailed.why: There is no map diagram type. The stops device draws an itinerary as a route motif, which is a line with labels, not a strait between two shores.

whatFailed.what: The causal chain -- one grounded tanker closes the lane, and every price moves -- is stated and never shown.
whatFailed.why: No representation for a blockage or a dependency; the rise motif on the price line is decoration, not consequence.

whatFailed.what: A plaque and a newspaper prop overlap on the closing shot.
